claims.claim: A single zero coefficient still defines a real-plane line.
claims.proof: For b=0, a!=0: x=-c/a, y arbitrary. For b!=0: y=-(a/b)x-c/b, x arbitrary. Both zero gives an identity or contradiction, not a line.

claims.claim: Decimal notation alone does not introduce a residual.
claims.proof: For a!=0 and exact solution s, residual at q is a(q-s). Thus q=s has zero residual even in terminating-decimal notation; 0.333 in 3x=1 gives -1/1000.

claims.claim: Reversible operations preserve the declared domain solution set.
claims.proof: Adding/subtracting the same defined term has an inverse; multiplication/division by a nonzero constant has an inverse. Multiplication by zero lacks this property.

claims.claim: An identity admits precisely the declared admissible domain.
claims.proof: After reversible reduction, the constant true equality holds for every admissible x; a false equality holds for none. Changing Q to R changes the domain, not the equality.

claims.claim: The denominator-clearing rule here is bounded to nonzero constant integer denominators.
claims.proof: Their positive LCM is nonzero, so multiplication has an inverse; variable denominators require additional domain restrictions outside this rule.
